audit.why: 51.11% over 90 games — the smallest sample in this slice, and diff EVEN / 6.0 is the honest read. A tank mirror where Sejuani owns the level-2 engage window and the late teamfight, and Cho'Gath owns 4-6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven stages are wrong, and the mirror entry (audits/top/sejuani__chogath.json) carries the IDENTICAL win array — both sides of this matchup were generated with the same broken chart, and the mirror audit recorded 'Neither chart needed moving', which was a miss. Sejuani's own whys[1] says 'your knock-up initiation outpaces his slow Rupture — step up and punish' while both arrays score Level 2 to Cho'Gath. Cho'Gath's whys[1] agrees it is Sejuani's ('out-trading you before your Q-W combo is reliable'). Same pattern at Levels 4-5, Level 6, First item and 2+ items.
audit.why: Reconciled against the packet chart and BOTH sides' whys text. Level 2 is Sejuani's: an 18-second, 650-range knock-up dash against a Cho'Gath with only Rupture. Levels 4-5 and 6 are Cho'Gath's: Vorpal Spikes on every auto, a Feral Scream that blanks the Permafrost cast, and a true-damage Feast that Frost Armor's resistances cannot blunt. 2+ items is Sejuani's: Glacial Prison is an AoE stun and Frost Armor's slow immunity turns off both of Cho'Gath's slows.
audit.corrected: Level 2 Sejuani (3/10), Level 3 Skill, Levels 4-5 Cho'Gath, Level 6 Cho'Gath (7/10), First item Skill, 2+ items Sejuani (3/10). Proposed as one atomic chart group across both layers, matching the packet exactly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page mislabels Sejuani's kit throughout and gets the core mechanic backwards. (a) Arctic Assault is called 'her W Arctic Assault dash' in five places — it is her Q. Winter's Wrath is W. (b) The page says the dash applies Frost. It does not: Riot's Arctic Assault text is only 'charges forward, knocking enemies into the air'. Frost stacks come from Winter's Wrath, and Permafrost stuns only a target at MAXIMUM Frost stacks. (c) Frost Armor is called a 'shield' in six places. It is not a shield — it grants Armor, Magic Resist, and IMMUNITY TO SLOWS. (d) Missing entirely: that slow immunity turns off both of Cho'Gath's slows (Rupture and Vorpal Spikes), and that Sejuani can damage a stunned enemy to shatter it for massive magic damage, which is what makes eating Permafrost lethal rather than merely inconvenient.
audit.why: Riot text — Fury of the North: 'Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows... Sejuani can damage a stunned enemy to shatter it, dealing massive magic damage.' Arctic Assault: Q, 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, 650 range, knock-up. Winter's Wrath: W, 9/8/7/6/5s, 600 range, 'slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks'. Permafrost: E, 1.5s, 560 range, 'stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks'. Glacial Prison: R, 120/105/90s, 1300 range.
audit.corrected: Slot letters corrected and the Winter's Wrath -> Permafrost stack chain stated in spikes[0].text, whys[1], wants.foe[0], early and report[5].t; Frost Armor rewritten as resistances plus slow immunity in wants.foe[1], whys[4], phases[4].why, phases[6].why and dontsFull[2]; the shatter-a-stunned-target burst added to dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire trading system is gated on Permafrost's cooldown — 'trade around Permafrost's cooldown', 'engage once it is down', 'Q-W while her stun is on cooldown'. Permafrost is 1.5 SECONDS. It is never down, so every one of those instructions is unactionable.
audit.why: This is the same defect the mirror agent found from Sejuani's side, where the page gated her step-ups on Rupture's 6-second flat cooldown. Here it is worse: 1.5s. The cooldowns that can actually be played around are Arctic Assault at 18s (bait the dash and she has no engage) and Winter's Wrath at 9s (no Winter's Wrath, no Frost stacks, no stun).
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d repointed to Arctic Assault's 18s and to denying Winter's Wrath stacks, with Permafrost's 1.5s stated explicitly so the reader stops waiting for it. phases[3].why carries the same correction.

edits.before: Two immobile tanks staring each other down — neither of you wins level 1, so just last-hit with Carnivore topping you off and feel out her cooldowns. The real danger is levels 2-3: her W Arctic Assault dash applies Frost, and an E Permafrost detonation stuns you, so she wins short trades before your Q-W combo is dependable and you have no escape if she walks you down. Do not throw a wide Rupture and step in to follow up — she just dashes in, stuns you with Permafrost, and chunks you. Soak with Carnivore sustain and accept a little chip; you both scale, so there is no rush.
edits.after: Two immobile tanks staring each other down — neither of you wins level 1, so just last-hit with Carnivore topping you off and feel out her cooldowns. The real danger is level 2: Arctic Assault (Q) is an 18-second dash that knocks you up, Winter's Wrath (W) fills your Frost gauge, and Permafrost (E) stuns once it is full — and she can then shatter a stunned target for massive magic damage. Do not throw a wide Rupture and step in to follow up. Bait the 18-second dash, soak with Carnivore, and accept a little chip; you both scale.
